key_insight: Pre-trained, off-the-shelf image-to-image generative models can remove imperceptible protective perturbations and recover usable images — no bespoke attack algorithms required.
problem_solved: Demonstrates that widely deployed image protection schemes (imperceptible perturbations designed to prevent style mimicry, deepfakes, or unauthorized reuse) can be defeated using standard image-to-image GenAI pipelines, revealing a gap between protection design and real-world threat models.
method: Feed protected images into off-the-shelf image-to-image generative models (no specialized attack training or custom architectures).
Leverage standard denoising/translation settings and simple prompt/control strategies to reconstruct images with protections removed.
Empirically evaluate the approach across multiple protection methods and datasets to show broad effectiveness.
impact: Indicates that many current image protection techniques are brittle in the face of readily available GenAI tools — practitioners must re-evaluate defenses, build provably robust protections, and update governance/usage policies accordingly.
visual_elements: Side-by-side before/after image pair: protected image (subtle perturbation overlay) → recovered image (clear content).
Pipeline diagram: protected image → off-the-shelf img2img model → recovered image, highlighting 'no custom attack' label.
Bar/line chart showing attack success rates across different protection schemes (specialized attack vs off-the-shelf model).
Icon set: broken shield (protection failure), model icon (GenAI), dataset stack (scale of impact).
paper_title: Off-The-Shelf Image-to-Image Models Are All You Need To Defeat Image Protection Schemes
paper_authors: Xavier Pleimling, Sifat Muhammad Abdullah, Gunjan Balde, Peng Gao, Mainack Mondal
